title: What Is White Label SEO? (2026 Guide)
excerpt: White label SEO explained: how agencies resell another company's SEO work under their own brand, what it includes, and what it costs.
description: What is white label SEO? It's SEO work one company performs that another resells under its own brand. Learn how the model works, what's included, and pricing.
tldr: White label SEO is search-engine-optimization work that one company performs but another — usually an agency — resells to clients under its own brand. The provider stays invisible; the client only ever sees the reselling agency. It lets agencies offer SEO without hiring an in-house team, and commonly includes audits, content, link building, and client-branded reports.

sections.heading: What is white label SEO?
body: The short answer to what is white label SEO is this: it is SEO work that one company performs but another company — usually a marketing agency — resells to its own clients under its own brand. The company doing the work stays invisible; the client believes the agency delivered everything in-house. The term "white label" borrows from retail, where a manufacturer makes a product with no branding so a retailer can sell it as their own.

In practice, three parties are involved: the **client** who wants SEO, the **agency** they hire, and the **white-label provider** the agency quietly subcontracts to. The provider audits the site, produces the content, builds the links, and writes the reports — then hands it all to the agency, who rebrands it and delivers it to the client as their own service.
Here is how that relationship flows:
[[flowchart]]

The defining feature is the branding. Everything the provider produces — reports, audits, deliverables — carries the agency's logo, not the provider's. If you have ever seen an agency offer SEO alongside web design and paid ads without a visible SEO department, there is a good chance a white-label partner is doing the work behind the scenes.

sections.heading: How white label SEO works (and white label vs. reseller)
body: White label SEO works as a behind-the-scenes fulfillment arrangement. The agency owns the client relationship — sales, strategy, communication, billing — while the provider owns execution. A typical cycle looks like this: the agency sends the client's site and goals to the provider; the provider runs an audit and proposes work; the agency approves and presents it as their own; the provider executes and reports; the agency relays results to the client. The client never learns the provider exists.
People often blur **white label** and **reseller** SEO, but there is a nuance worth knowing:
- **White label** means the service is unbranded so the agency can fully rebrand it as their own. The agency usually stays involved in strategy and client communication.

- **Reseller** means the agency simply resells a provider's packaged service, sometimes with lighter involvement. Reseller programs may or may not be fully white-labeled — some carry the provider's branding.

In everyday use the terms overlap heavily, and many providers use them interchangeably. The practical question to ask a partner is not "is this white label or reseller" but "can I put my logo on every deliverable and stay the only face the client sees?" If yes, it functions as white label regardless of the label on the program.

sections.heading: What white label SEO includes, and what it costs
body: White label SEO covers the same work a full in-house team would, packaged for resale. The most common deliverables are:
- **Technical and SEO audits** — a full crawl of the client's site flagging crawlability, speed, metadata, and structured-data issues, delivered as a branded report.
- **Content** — keyword-targeted blog posts, landing pages, and on-page optimization written to the client's topics.
- **Link building** — outreach, digital PR, and backlink acquisition to grow off-page authority.
- **Reporting** — recurring dashboards and PDF summaries, rebranded with the agency's logo, that the agency forwards to the client.

**White-label reports are the single most common entry point.** Even agencies with some in-house skill often outsource just the reporting, because branding a professional audit as your own is fast, cheap, and impressive to clients. You can do exactly this for free: run any client URL through the [free SEO + GEO audit on the homepage](/) and export a clean, white-label PDF report to present under your own brand — no signup, no provider logo.

On pricing, white label SEO usually runs on monthly retainers. Individual deliverables like a one-off audit or a batch of articles are cheaper, while ongoing full-service retainers cost more; the agency then marks up whatever the provider charges before billing the client. Because rates vary widely by scope and market, benchmark against the general ranges in [how much does SEO cost](/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost) and confirm the markup leaves you a healthy margin.

sections.heading: Pros, cons, and who white label SEO is for
body: White label SEO is mainly for **agencies that want to offer SEO without building an in-house team** — web-design shops, PPC agencies, and full-service marketing firms whose clients keep asking for SEO. It lets them say yes, add a revenue line, and keep clients from wandering to a competitor, all without hiring specialists or buying enterprise tools.
Here is the honest trade-off:

> Upside: you scale SEO capacity instantly, keep overhead low, and present a complete service. Downside: you sacrifice some control, depend on a partner's quality, and earn thinner margins than doing the work yourself.

The specific pros are speed and flexibility — you can take on SEO clients immediately and scale up or down without payroll risk — plus access to specialist tools and expertise you would otherwise have to buy. The cons are real too: quality is only as good as your provider, communication runs through an extra layer that can slow fixes, and margins shrink because someone else takes a cut. Vet a partner carefully by testing their audits and content before you put a client's name on them.

If you are an agency, a smart middle path is to keep the high-visibility, trust-building work in-house — strategy, client-facing audits, and reporting you control — while white-labeling the labor-intensive parts like bulk content and link outreach. Start by running your own free audits so the first deliverable a client sees is branded, credible, and entirely yours. To understand what you are reselling, brush up with [what is SEO and how it works](/blog/what-is-seo-and-how-it-works) and [how to do an SEO audit](/blog/how-to-do-an-seo-audit).

peopleAlsoAsk.a: White label SEO is SEO work that one company performs but another — usually a marketing agency — resells to clients under its own brand. The provider does the audits, content, links, and reporting behind the scenes and delivers everything unbranded, so the agency can add its own logo and present the service as in-house. The client never learns the provider exists.

peopleAlsoAsk.q: How does white label SEO work?
peopleAlsoAsk.a: White label SEO works as a three-party arrangement: the client hires the agency, the agency subcontracts a white-label provider, and the provider executes the SEO work behind the scenes. The provider delivers unbranded audits, content, links, and reports; the agency rebrands them and presents the results to the client as its own. The agency owns the relationship while the provider owns execution.

peopleAlsoAsk.q: What is the difference between white label and reseller SEO?
peopleAlsoAsk.a: White label SEO is unbranded so an agency can fully rebrand it as its own, usually staying involved in strategy and client communication. Reseller SEO means simply reselling a provider's packaged service, sometimes with lighter involvement and sometimes carrying the provider's branding. The terms overlap heavily in practice; the real question is whether you can put your logo on every deliverable and stay the client's only point of contact.

peopleAlsoAsk.q: How much does white label SEO cost?
peopleAlsoAsk.a: White label SEO usually runs on monthly retainers, with one-off deliverables like a single audit or batch of articles costing less than ongoing full-service work. The agency marks up whatever the provider charges before billing the client. Prices vary widely by scope and market, so benchmark against general SEO pricing ranges and confirm the markup leaves a healthy margin. White-label reporting alone can be done for free.

peopleAlsoAsk.q: Is white label SEO worth it?
peopleAlsoAsk.a: White label SEO is worth it for agencies that want to offer SEO without hiring an in-house team, because it adds a revenue line and scales instantly with low overhead. The trade-offs are less control, dependence on the partner's quality, and thinner margins. It is worth it when you vet the provider carefully and keep high-trust, client-facing work — like strategy and branded reports — under your own control.

faqs.q: Can I white label an SEO audit report for free?
faqs.a: Yes. Run a client's URL through a free SEO and GEO audit, then export the results as a clean PDF with no provider branding and present it under your own logo. This is the fastest, cheapest form of white label SEO and a common first deliverable agencies use to win a client's trust.

faqs.q: Do clients know their agency uses white label SEO?
faqs.a: Usually not, and that is the point of the model. White label deliverables are unbranded so the agency can present them as in-house work, and the client typically never learns a provider was involved. Some agencies disclose it anyway; whether to do so is an ethical and relationship choice, not a technical requirement.

faqs.q: Is white label SEO only for agencies?
faqs.a: Mostly, but not exclusively. Agencies are the primary users because they resell it to clients under their own brand. Freelancers and consultants also use white-label providers to handle work outside their expertise, and even some in-house teams outsource labor-heavy tasks like link building or content while keeping strategy internal.
